## Personality

Jane Andrews is described as a plain, steady, and sensible individual whose unflappable nature keeps her from being easily rattled. She possesses a lady-like, neat, and practical demeanor, working as a conscientious and plodding student who earned honors in domestic science for her strong cooking abilities. Although she originally aimed to study for Queen's [Entrance](../codex/places.md#entrance) examination and envisioned devoting her entire life to teaching, she eventually resigns from the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) school to head West in the fall. As a teacher, her strict approach of punishing pupils for funny speeches makes the work monotonous, even though she strives to earn her salary fairly, satisfy the trustees, and secure a place on the School Inspector's roll of honor. Now engaged to a millionaire, her main difficulty is that her husband will not allow her to cook despite her high skill in it.

## History

Jane Andrews grew up in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) as a friend of [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md), joining a schoolgirl [Story Club](../codex/factions.md#story-club) with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md), and Ruby in their schooldays. She later attended a benefit concert at the [White Sands Hotel](../codex/places.md#white-sands-hotel) with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Billy Andrews](../character/billy-andrews.md). After finishing her schooling, Jane took up teaching at the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) school. Outside of teaching, she remained involved in community affairs, gathering with her friends after a hall-painting disaster and joining [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md), and [Priscilla](../character/priscilla-grant.md) on a spring picnic walk to [Hester](../character/hester-gray.md) Gray's garden. As part of a committee for the Village [Improvement Society](../codex/factions.md#improvers) alongside [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md), she unsuccessfully attempted to persuade [Judson Parker](../character/judson-parker.md) not to rent his fences for advertisements. Jane eventually resigned from her position at the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) school to teach on the western prairies. Before going West, she visited [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) at [Redmond College](../codex/places.md#redmond-college) to propose to her on behalf of her shy brother, [Billy Andrews](../character/billy-andrews.md); when [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) refused the proposal, Jane responded coldly.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert P1](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0001), [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert P28](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0028), [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert P33](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0033), [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert P34](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0034), [v2 IX A Question of Color P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000), [v2 IX A Question of Color P24](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0024), +21 more_

## Quotes

> "Wouldn’t it be nice to have three wishes granted you . . . or even only one? What would you wish for, girls, if you could have a wish granted? I’d wish to be rich and beautiful and clever."
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v2 XIII A Golden Picnic P32](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0032)

> “I don’t know how you’re going to prevent him,” exclaimed Jane bitterly. “Everybody knows what Judson Parker is. He’d do anything for money. He hasn’t a spark of public spirit or any sense of the beautiful.”
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v2 XIV A Danger Averted P41](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0041)

> “Of course it would be romantic,” conceded Jane Andrews, “but I know I couldn’t keep still. I’d be popping up every minute or so to see where I was and if I wasn’t drifting too far out. And you know, Anne, that would spoil the effect.”
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v1 CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid P2](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0002)

> “Oh, Anne,” gasped Jane, as they fled to the girls’ dressing room amid hearty cheers. “Oh, Anne I’m so proud! Isn’t it splendid?”
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream P8](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0008)

> "I’ll whip my pupils when they’re naughty. It’s the shortest and easiest way of convincing them."
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v2 IV Different Opinions P14](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0014)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--jane-andrews.md)

Jane and [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) are longtime friends and travel companions who both attended Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#queen-s-academy) and became fellow teachers. They share many childhood memories together, including participating in local concerts and story clubs, as well as attending school events under Miss [Stacy](../character/stacy.md). During a outing to a concert at the [White Sands Hotel](../codex/places.md#white-sands-hotel), Jane traveled with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and supported her through her performance.
